text:
maria: Noticed a customer ticket reporting p95 latency jump to ~2.4s after today's runtime canary roll (v2.3.7). They say it started around 09:45 UTC. Canary traffic was ~10%
kevin: saw the alert earlier, p95 for gen-route spiked across that cohort. p50 unchanged. p99 small bump but noisy.
lee: ops-bot traces show tail spans concentrated on kernel_selector_v5 and batch scheduler queueing. linking perf dashboard: https://redwood.prod/dashboards/123
sophia: customer says requests that used to complete ~600ms are timing at ~2s for some payloads (long-ish prompts). They reported no auth errors or 429s, just slower completions.
maria: quick hypothesis: selector v5 routing + slightly larger default batch sizes for long seqs. We rolled selector_v5 to canary earlier today. Can we confirm change list?
kevin: confirmed: rollout included kernel selector tweak + kv-cache TTL change (from 30s->5s) for memory reclaim. I pushed metrics comparison in #release-notes. suspecting batch packing behavior changed due to TTL.
lee: repro steps I ran locally (small canary cluster):
```
# reproduce load pattern
wrk -t4 -c50 -d60s --script=long_prompt.lua https://canary-runtime.prod/gen
kubectl logs -l app=runtime-canary -n runtime | grep "batch.size"
```
I reproduced p95 ~2.1s with selector_v5 + TTL=5s but p95 ~650ms when switching back to selector_v4 + TTL=30s.
kevin: interesting. traces show more frequent cold KV cache misses which cause extra key fetches and requeueing for long sequences. That aligns with increased per-request duration.
maria: options: 1) throttle canary rollout (scale down canary weight to 1-2%), 2) revert kernel selector change in canary, 3) revert TTL change, 4) short-term mitigation: reduce max_batch_size for canary pods to reduce queueing. Thoughts?
sophia: customer impact is moderate (affecting mid-tier accounts). They asked for ETA to fix. Recommend immediate throttle + rollback to selector_v4 for canary while we bisect TTL impact.
lee: I'll throttle canary to 2% now and open a rollback PR for selector_v4. Also will push a hotpatch to set max_batch_size=8 for canary pods as a quick mitigation.
kevin: I'll run a controlled A/B with TTL toggled back to 30s on a small cohort to confirm root cause. If reverting TTL alone fixes it we can keep selector_v5 and adjust cache config.
maria: plan sounds good. Action items:
- lee: throttle canary + apply batch-size hotpatch (doing now)
- lee: open rollback PR for selector if mitigation fails (T: 30m)
- kevin: run TTL A/B and post perf delta + traces (T: 45m)
- sophia: update customer with interim mitigation and ETA (~1h)
- maria: coordinate postmortem and test matrix (kernel vs TTL vs batch)

lee: throttled canary -> 2%, applied batch-size=8 hotpatch, monitoring...
ops-bot: alert suppressed for eng-runtime p95 surge (silenced by lee)
kevin: early numbers after hotpatch: p95 for canary cohort dropped from 2.4s -> 820ms in first 5m. p99 trending down. Traces show fewer KV miss spikes.
sophia: replied to customer: "We've throttled canary traffic and applied a mitigation; engineering is investigating root cause. We'll follow up with timeline after bisecting changes"
maria: good work. keep channel updated. we'll decide rollback if numbers don't stabilize in next 20-30m.
kevin: if TTL reversion alone reproduces improvement we should consider making 30s default until we have a KV eviction strategy.
lee: opening rollback PR now in case. link: https://git.redwood/pr/4523
maria: thanks all. I'll start a short incident note and tag postmortem template.
